common_name: Butterfly Deep Pink Pentas (Heat-Proof Rose-Pink Star-Cluster Hummingbird Plant)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Butterfly Deep Pink holds a saturated rose-pink color through the summer heat that washes out many pastel pentas selections.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost. Butterfly Deep Pink carries dense, rounded umbels of star-shaped florets in a saturated rose-pink that reads noticeably deeper and warmer than the soft blush of 'Butterfly Pink' already grown in the series. The tall, upright habit and large flower clusters make it one of the more substantial pentas for back-of-border color, and the nonstop bloom holds up through the peak of Gulf Coast summer heat when many bedding annuals stall. Deadheading is unnecessary since spent umbels are quickly hidden by new growth. Butterflies, sulphurs, and hummingbirds work the flower heads steadily from planting through the first hard freeze.
sources: PanAmerican Seed Pentas Butterfly series trial notes

common_name: Butterfly Light Lavender Pentas (Heat-Proof Pale Lavender Star-Cluster Pollinator Plant)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; the pale lavender flower color is a softer, cooler tone than the standard 'Butterfly Lavender' selection already grown.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost. Butterfly Light Lavender produces large, showy corymbs of pale lavender star-shaped flowers from late spring through mid-fall, a noticeably softer and cooler tone than the richer purple-lavender of the standard 'Butterfly Lavender' cultivar already in cultivation. The tall, upright growth habit and drought tolerance once established make it useful for mixed borders where a muted pastel accent is wanted among brighter bedding colors. Like other members of the Butterfly series, it flowers continuously through the harshest part of the Gulf Coast summer and draws swallowtails, sulphurs, and hummingbirds in steady numbers.
sources: PanAmerican Seed Pentas Butterfly series trial notes

common_name: Butterfly Red Pentas (Heat-Proof True Red Star-Cluster Hummingbird Plant)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Butterfly Red is a brighter, truer scarlet than the wine-toned 'Butterfly Deep Red' already grown, with prominent white anthers that make the flower clusters pop against the foliage.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after the last frost. Butterfly Red bears large, rounded clusters of vivid true-red star-shaped flowers accented by contrasting white anthers, a brighter and more scarlet tone than the deeper wine-red of 'Butterfly Deep Red' already in the collection. The tall, vigorous habit produces an abundance of flower heads that remain hummingbird magnets throughout the growing season, and plants keep flowering through the hottest, most humid stretch of the Gulf Coast summer with no pause. Site in mass plantings near patios or windows for close-up hummingbird viewing.
sources: Ball Seed Pentas Butterfly series trial notes

common_name: Kaleidoscope Appleblossom Pentas (Early-Blooming Pale Pink and Rose Bicolor Pentas)

planting.note: Transplant after last frost into warm soil; Kaleidoscope Appleblossom is one of the earliest pentas selections to bloom, flowering noticeably sooner from a young transplant than most other dwarf pentas.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, fertile soil, watering regularly until established. Kaleidoscope Appleblossom is a dwarf, mounded selection distinguished by soft bicolor flower clusters that combine pale blush pink with a deeper rose center within the same umbel, giving the plant a two-toned, almost variegated look in bloom rather than the single flat color of 'Kaleidoscope Red' already grown. It is among the earliest of the Kaleidoscope series to come into flower and holds a tidy, compact shape all season, making it well suited to containers and the front of a sunny border. Expect strong butterfly and hummingbird traffic from spring through the first fall frost.
sources: Benary cultivar reference — Pentas lanceolata F1 Kaleidoscope Appleblossom

common_name: Silver Mound Trailing Lantana (Creamy White Gold-Eyed Mounding Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Silver Mound rarely sets berries, so nearly all of its energy goes into an unusually dense, continuous flush of flowers rather than seed production.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun after the last frost date. Silver Mound grows as a dense, tidy mound rather than the long trailing runners typical of most Lantana montevidensis selections, covering itself in creamy white flower clusters with a small gold eye from spring through fall. The compact, rounded habit and free-flowering, largely seedless nature make it a tidier choice than the species form for foundation plantings, low borders, and mass color beds where a sprawling groundcover habit is not wanted. Like other trailing lantana, it is highly heat- and drought-tolerant once established and draws steady butterfly activity through the growing season; expect dieback to the crown in hard freezes at the cold end of its range with vigorous spring regrowth.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Gardening Solutions — Lantana

common_name: Patriot Rainbow Lantana (Dwarf Multicolor Pink-Orange-Gold Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Patriot Rainbow is among the smallest lantana cultivars available, making it well suited to containers and small-scale bedding where the larger Patriot series selections would be oversized.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Patriot Rainbow is a diminutive selection from the Patriot breeding series, forming a tight, low mound only about a foot tall and wide, densely packed with flower clusters that open pale yellow and shift through vivid pink, orange, and gold as they age, so a single cluster shows several colors at once. Its extremely free-flowering habit and small stature make it one of the better lantana choices for tucking into rock gardens, edging, and mixed containers where full-size lantana cultivars would quickly overwhelm the space. Like other lantana, it shrugs off heat and drought once established and is a steady butterfly draw all summer.
sources: Monrovia — Patriot Rainbow Compact Lantana plant profile
Devil Mountain Wholesale Nursery cultivar reference

common_name: Patriot Desert Sunset Lantana (Upright Mounding Orange-Gold-Coral Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Desert Sunset's upright, mounding habit reaches a substantial 3 feet in a single season, making it more of a small flowering shrub than a bedding lantana.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Patriot Desert Sunset grows as a vigorous, upright mound reaching roughly three feet tall and wide in a single growing season, considerably larger and more shrub-like than compact Patriot series selections such as 'Patriot Rainbow'. Flower clusters combine warm orange, gold, pink, and coral tones in the same umbel, echoing the colors of a desert sunset and shifting further as individual florets age. The bold color and substantial size make it useful as a seasonal flowering hedge or backdrop planting, and it flowers without pause through the peak of Gulf Coast summer heat, drawing butterflies in large numbers.
sources: Devil Mountain Wholesale Nursery — Lantana Patriot Desert Sunset plant profile

common_name: Patriot Marc Cathey Lantana (Vigorous Sterile White-and-Yellow Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container plants after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; Patriot Marc Cathey is sterile and puts on remarkably vigorous growth, reaching up to 5 feet tall and wide in a single season.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost date. Patriot Marc Cathey is a large, vigorous, mounding selection from the Patriot breeding series, capable of reaching roughly five feet tall and wide in a single growing season under Gulf Coast heat. Flower clusters are clean white with a clear lemon-yellow center, a crisper and more luminous color combination than the muted cream tones of many older white lantana selections. Because the cultivar is sterile, it channels its energy into an exceptionally heavy, continuous bloom rather than seed production, and requires no deadheading. Its size makes it better suited to use as a seasonal flowering shrub or informal hedge than as a small-bed bedding plant, and it draws butterflies steadily from planting through the first hard freeze.
sources: Garden.org plant database — Lantana camara Patriot series
